events.title: Vernissage
events.descEN:
We are pleased to invite you to the opening reception of the final exhibition of the research project SENTIMENT on December 11, 2026, at 6:00 PM at Kunstwerk Köln.

Through films, installations, textile works, performances, sound pieces, and other media-based formats, participating artists offer audiences an experiential entry point for engaging with complex and often intangible topics. Their artistic research explores vulnerability, intimacy, and the handling of personal data. The works inhabit the intersection of digitality, human connection, and the discourses that shape our contemporary moment.
events.descDE:
Wir laden ein zur Vernissage der abschließenden Ausstellung des Forschungsprojekts SENTIMENT am 11.12.2026 um 18:00 Uhr im Kunstwerk Köln.

Mit Filmen, Installationen, Textilarbeiten, Performances, Soundpieces und anderen medialen Umsetzungen bieten Kunstschaffende Betrachtenden eine erlebbare Ebene, über schwer greifbare Thematiken in Austausch zu kommen. Ihre künstlerische Forschung thematisiert Verletzlichkeit, Intimität und den Umgang mit privaten Daten. Die Arbeiten bewegen sich im Spannungsfeld von Digitalität, Nähe und den Diskursen, die unsere Gegenwart prägen.

program.descDE: Die Eröffnung wird durch eine Begrüßung und ein gemeinsames Grußwort der Forschenden des Projekts SENTIMENT eingeleitet. Im Anschluss laden wir zu Austausch und Begegnung bei einem Empfang mit Getränken und kleinen Speisen ein.
program.descEN: The opening will begin with a welcome and a joint address by the researchers of the SENTIMENT project. This will be followed by an opportunity for exchange and encounter at a reception with food and drinks.

program.descDE: Die Performance findet im Ausstellungsraum als visuelle und audiovisuelle Intervention statt. Sie entfaltet sich in direkter Auseinandersetzung mit den installierten Arbeiten und dem räumlichen Kontext.
program.descEN: The performance will take place within the exhibition space as a visual and audiovisual intervention. It unfolds directly in relation to the installed works and the surrounding spatial context.

program.descDE: Ein gemeinsames Gathering mit einem audiovisuellen Intermezzo zwischen Radiokunst und performativem Erzählen eröffnet einen Rahmen für kollektives Erleben und lädt zur gemeinsamen Begegnung und zum Austausch ein.
program.descEN: A shared gathering with an audiovisual intermezzo between radio art and performative storytelling opens a framework for collective experience and invites encounter and exchange.

events.title: Engineered for Intimacy: An Ethicsâ€“Privacyâ€“Psychology Dialogue on Intimate AI
events.descEN:
What happens when we open up to a machine? As AI-based dialogue systems become confidants, companions, and even romantic partners, they raise entangled questions across disciplines: Why do we form emotional bonds with chatbots? What happens to the intimate data we share with them? And what do designers, companies, and society owe the people who trust them?

This public panel brings three perspectives into conversation â€” psychology, privacy and security research, and ethics â€” to explore intimate communication between humans and AI. Set within the SENTIMENT exhibition, where scientific research meets artistic practice, the discussion situates these questions in a space designed to make them tangible, debatable, and shared.

Over 90 minutes, our speakers will trade perspectives and take questions from the audience, followed by an informal gathering to continue the conversation directly with the panelists. Free and open to all.

The speakers

Representing the SENTIMENT project:

Dr. Jessica Szczuka (Psychology, University of Duisburg-Essen) researches how people form emotional and intimate connections with AI and other technologies, and represents the project's psychological perspective.

Prof. Dr. Veelasha Moonsamy (Computer Science / Privacy, Ruhr University Bochum) researches user data privacy, privacy engineering and compliance, and applications of machine learning for security and privacy, and represents the project's computer science perspective.

Invited guest speakers:

Rongjun Ma (Privacy / Human-AI Interaction, Aalto University) studies privacy, boundaries, and personal agency in human-AI relationships, including intimate and romantic ones, asking what control people retain over what they share.

Prof. Dr. Eva Weber-Guskar (Ethics, Ruhr University Bochum) works on the ethics of emotions and artificial intelligence, examining the moral questions raised when machines enter our emotional and relational lives.

infoCards.body_en:
What happens when people begin to trust machines â€” or confide in them? At a time when AI is increasingly becoming our most trusted conversation partner, these encounters have become a matter of urgent social concern.

Funded by the BMFTR, SENTIMENT examines intimate communication with AI-based chatbots at the intersection of psychology, computer science, law, and artistic research. Installation, performance, and discursive formats make the central questions around this topic tangible.

SENTIMENT navigates the boundaries between connection and calculus: asking not only why people confide in AI but how intimacy can be designed without compromising autonomy.
